title: Is the sum of any three such numbers a multiple of six?
description: {{NAME_4}} has written numbers that leave remainder two on division by six and claims that any three of them add to a multiple of six. The video writes each number as six times its rows plus two, adds them, and checks the claim.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the full rows and the loose remainders separately, and see what the loose part makes. Watch for students who test one set of three numbers and call the claim proved.

source: Figure it Out (multiples and remainders, question 6)
video_script.why: The student can add remainders as the book's example does for two numbers and now adds three numbers to test a claim.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as six times its rows plus two, add the rows and the loose parts separately, then check with real numbers.
video_script.anchor: dots laid in rows of six, with two loose dots beside the full rows, as in the book's pictures of remainders
video_script.payoff_line: The three remainders of two make six

final_answer.value: Yes, the claim is true: the three remainders of 2 make 6
final_answer.spoken: yes, the claim is true because the three remainders of two make six

names.{{NAME_4}}: the child who claims that three numbers with remainder 2 on division by 6 add to a multiple of 6

maths_rules: the numbers are 6p + 2, 6q + 2 and 6r + 2 with p, q, r whole numbers
video_script.design: Dots in rows of six with two loose. Three such piles are added, the rows together and the loose dots together; the loose dots make one more row.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; several numbers each shown as rows of six dots with two loose; a speech card with the claim: the sum of any three is a multiple of 6

marks.named: the piles of dots appear, each in rows of six with two loose
marks.claim: the claim appears on a speech card
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the claim

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='named'/>{{NAME_4}} has written several numbers that leave remainder two on division by six.
<bookmark mark='claim'/>{{NAME_4}} claims that the sum of any three such numbers is always a multiple of six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is the claim true?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three piles of dots, each in full rows of six with 2 dots loose

marks.same: the words the same way as the example in your book appear
marks.piles: each pile shows full rows of six with two dots loose
marks.three: the three piles move side by side, rows with rows and loose dots with loose dots

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='piles'/>Each such number is full rows of six, with two dots loose.
<bookmark mark='three'/>We add three of them, the full rows together and the loose dots together.

beats.on_screen: Given: three numbers, each leaves remainder 2 on division by 6
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, each of three numbers leaves remainder two on division by six.

beats.on_screen: To find: is the sum of the three numbers always a multiple of 6?

marks.find: the question to settle is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find if their sum is always a multiple of six.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the numbers are 6p + 2, 6q + 2 and 6r + 2, with p, q, r whole numbers

marks.write: each number is written as six times its rows plus two
marks.letters: the letters p, q and r are written for the rows of the three numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write each number as six times its rows, plus two.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>Use p, q and r for the rows. The numbers are six p plus two, six q plus two, and six r plus two.

marks.add: the three numbers are added, with the rows and the loose parts grouped
marks.loose: the loose parts two, two and two join to make six

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the three numbers. The rows are six p, six q and six r.
<bookmark mark='loose'/>The loose parts are two, two and two, which make six.

marks.factor: six is taken out of every part of the sum
marks.whole: the bracket p plus q plus r plus one is marked as a whole number

narration: <bookmark mark='factor'/>Step three, six divides every part, so take six out.
The sum is six times the number p plus q plus r plus one.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>That number is a whole number, because p, q and r are whole numbers.

marks.nums: two, eight and fourteen are each split into rows of six with two over
marks.total: their sum, twenty four, is split into four rows of six

narration: <bookmark mark='nums'/>Step four, check with two, eight and fourteen. Each leaves remainder two on division by six.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Their sum is twenty four, which is six times four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes, the claim is true: the three remainders of 2 make 6
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, the claim is true.
The three remainders of two make six, so the sum is a multiple of six.
